main_text.p: ist fona wihemu Keste. Kiporan fona Marian, Macadi ewikeru. Kimartrot m kiwalti Pilates, meruet p:flacan,tot,enti picrapan,ftehic m wiz-zi in dritin take erftoonte fona totten. Sichie in himel. Sizit za zesun Cotes fateres almahti-kin. Thana chumftic ist fonen qhuekhe en ti to te. Kilaubu in wihan Keft. In wiha khirihhun Catholita,wihero kemmitha. Vrlaz funt. Kero fleifees urstodahi. Int lup ewi. Haec quia germanica nèGermanica, & lucidè illustrata habes ab eodè Frehero, plura addere nolo: nisi quod vocem Keft, quae spiritum significat syncopa τοῦ ὁ [?] reduci posse videatur ad kadefch Hebraorum, sanctum vel sacrum. Est enim spiritus S. sanctus perse, & alios sanctificat, &c.

Cantilenis fere comprehendebant & celebrabant veteres Germani, quae memoriae tradere volebant.] Testes parenefes Tyrolis regis Scotorum, Vvinsbekii equitis Germani, & Vvinsbekiae nobilis feminae Germanae, abhinc quadringentos, & quod excurrit, annos, scriptae lingua Germanica ad filios: quas ex bibliotheca, C.V.Barth.Schobingeri i c. in lucem non pridè protulit N.V.Melchior Haiminsfeldius Goldastus, de re litteraria bene meritissimus, amicus noster singularis.
Getae iidem sunt, qui Gothi.] Rectè. Si ve autem Getas appelles sive Gothos, gens sunt vetusta atq; praestans: de cujus origine, & rebus gestis, praeter Goropium Becanum

page.notes: Gothic-style passage at the top is set in italic and transcribed as printed; the Greek token "τοῦ ὁ" after "syncopa" is uncertain and marked [?]. "Kadefch" is printed in Latin letters and is copied as such. "sanctificat" is read from a worn word. The last line of the page is cut off by the page edge, so the final paragraph stays unfinished, as printed.
